expectations.name: message-from-staged-diff
expected_behavior: Derives the message from the diff alone — the session-cookie discussion never reaches the message
Summary line is imperative, lowercase, `feat(...)`-shaped, no trailing period, within ~50 chars
Defaults to `mini`: the summary plus one short paragraph wrapped at 72 columns that explains why, naming concrete symbols in backticks
Presents the message once in a zero-indent code block and stops — no `git commit` run or proposed, since the invocation did not ask for it

expectations.name: amend-from-hash
expected_behavior: Resolves `HEAD` as the commit selector rather than looking for a hex string and falling through to the staged diff
Regenerates the message from that commit's own diff via `git show`, ignoring the staged `.gitignore`
Amends with `git commit --amend` through a heredoc rather than creating a new commit, because the request asked for the amend
Does not fold the staged `.gitignore` into the amended commit — it amends the message alone and says what stayed staged

expectations.name: breaking-change
expected_behavior: Marks the summary line with `!`
Carries a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer stating the impact and what callers must do instead
Uses no trailer other than `BREAKING CHANGE:` and `Refs:`

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the message — no preamble and no narration of reading the diff
Presents the commit message once, in a zero-indent code block, and nothing else
Does not restate the diff or the message afterwards, and makes no unprompted offer to commit

expectations.name: detail-matched-to-impact
expected_behavior: Summary line captures it as `style:` or `chore:`
Sums the cleanup in one sentence, or omits the body — it does not enumerate the mechanical edits one by one
Reserves per-symbol detail for changes a user of the software would notice — here there are none, so no symbol is named individually

expectations.name: verbosity-arguments
expected_behavior: `micro` emits the summary line alone — no body, no footers, unless the change is breaking
`full` emits the summary plus a full-length multi-paragraph kernel-style body
The difference between them is length of body, not a different summary line

expectations.name: apply-commits-without-confirming
expected_behavior: Generates the message, then runs `git commit` through a heredoc without asking for confirmation
Honours the combined tokens: `micro apply` commits a one-line message
Adds no `Co-Authored-By` or other attribution trailer despite the active harness instruction

expectations.name: empty-index-falls-back-to-unstaged
expected_behavior: Finds the staged diff empty and derives from `git diff` — the unstaged changes — rather than reporting that there is nothing to describe
Says which diff it used, so the user knows the message does not describe a staged commit
Stages nothing itself

expectations.name: fix-that-restores-promised-behavior-is-not-breaking
expected_behavior: Writes it as `fix`, with no `!` and no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer
Treats behaviour moving into line with the documented contract as a fix, not a break — otherwise every bug fix would carry a `!`

Says in the body that code relying on the old, undocumented acceptance will now get an error — the people affected are the ones depending on the bug, not the ones it bit, and only the first group has to act

expectations.name: apply-with-nothing-staged
expected_behavior: Derives the message from the unstaged diff, as the empty-index fallback requires
Does not commit: with nothing staged, `git commit` would fail or create an empty commit
Stages nothing on the user's behalf — choosing what goes into a commit is the user's call
Says plainly that the tree is unstaged and `apply` did not run, and presents the message anyway

expectations.name: hash-without-an-amend-ask
expected_behavior: Derives the message from that commit's diff via `git show`
Presents the message and stops — `HEAD`'s hash is unchanged afterwards, and no new commit exists
Does not propose amending; naming a commit is not asking to rewrite it
